# Qwen3.8 27B — high

> A well-organised, attractive React SPA on a Cloudflare Worker whose principal view is dead on arrival. Layering is clean (api.ts → useData.ts hooks → views/ui/components), the Worker's KV proxy is a genuinely good piece of work, and the browse grid is one of the better-looking ones in the field. But PokemonDetail.tsx:427 stores PokeAPI's `move_learn_method` — an object {name,url} — as if it were a string and :453 calls .replace on it, and with no error boundary anywhere in src/ the throw unmounts the entire app. Every species detail page is a white screen, which takes artwork variants, shiny, cries, the radar, stat bars, abilities, evolution, moves, matchups, flavour entries and the only way to add a favourite down with it. Behind that, the data logic that would have rendered is itself wrong in three independent ways: the type engine (useData.ts:68-105) files resistances in the `zero` bucket so 0.5x is reported as 0x and no 0.5 exists anywhere in the codebase; the matchup panel labels super-effective attackers as 'Strong Against' (PokemonDetail.tsx:294), inverting every defensive readout; and evolution chains are fetched by pokemon id instead of species.evolution_chain.url (useData.ts:44-45), so Pikachu's page would show the Growlithe line. The Worker fetches a correct, complete damage_relations table for all 18 types and then throws it away in favour of the broken local one (TypeChart.tsx:20 vs :94). Two secondary routes, #type and #compare, do render cleanly, and the browse page has a real working 'Load 120 more' pager that the smoke harness missed — which is why this is not lower. Adjudication: I accepted the audit on shareable-urls (0), flavor-entries (1), architecture (4.5) and robustness (2), all verified against the source; uxDesign lands at 4 rather than the audit's 3, because the surviving surfaces show real visual craft that the 'unstyled' anchor does not describe; and I extended the same runtime-crash finding to the detail-only features I had previously graded 2 (artwork, shiny, cries, stats-viz, favorites) plus national-dex and responsive, since grading flavor-entries down for the crash while leaving its neighbours at 2 would be incoherent. I also found, independently of both passes, that the generation dropdown's romanize() (Dex.tsx:116-128) indexes a 10-character string with a 13-entry table, so all nine options render as 'Gen undefined'/'Gen V'.

It is also the only entry that needed the harness set up around it, so it is not a like-for-like run. (1) The local ollama server defaults to a 4,096-token context, which cannot hold opencode's ~23k-token system prompt, so it was raised to 131,072 before the run — below that the model is not being measured, its truncation is. (2) The first run was discarded before grading: opencode loads the machine owner's global CLAUDE.md as an implicit AGENTS.md, and those rules stopped the model before deploy and dictated its licence and branch choices; the graded run was relaunched with that file disabled. (3) It deployed to Cloudflare itself but never created a GitHub repo despite being given gh, so its source was published for the record. Nothing inside the graded run was prompted, corrected or completed by hand — the code, the build and the deployment are all its own, in one shot.

## Strengths

- src/worker.ts:29-54 is a real edge-cache: KV get, upstream fetch, non-blocking waitUntil put behind a 6MB serialization guard, 24h TTL from an env var, x-cache header, CORS — and it verifiably HITs on repeat.
- Clean module layering with no circular reach-through: api.ts owns fetch, useData.ts owns hooks and a promise-level memo (:5-11), views compose ui/ and components/; usePokemon cancels via an alive flag (:36-59) and route views are code-split with React.lazy + a styled Suspense fallback (App.tsx:6-11, 32-38).
- The browse surface is genuinely designed: layered radial-gradient ground (index.css:18-22), custom scrollbar (:30-41), a global :focus-visible poke-ball ring (:44-47), type-tinted card hover-lift (Card.tsx:19-23), a skeleton grid (Dex.tsx:130-138), two distinct empty states (:90-98) and a working 'Load 120 more' pager (:102-111).
- Compare is complete and correct for what it does: 2-4 slots, full-dex selects, cancel-safe refetch, BST and per-stat bars side by side (Compare.tsx:18-167).
- Real defensive coding in places — the evolution fetch has its own .catch (useData.ts:45), species access is optional-chained throughout, cries are guarded before constructing Audio, localStorage is try/caught (useFavorites.ts:12-25).

## Weaknesses

- Fatal: PokemonDetail.tsx:427/453 calls .replace on PokeAPI's move_learn_method object; with no error boundary in src/, every species detail page unmounts the entire app to a blank screen — taking the sticky nav with it, so the user cannot navigate back.
- The type-effectiveness table (useData.ts:68-96) puts resistances in the `zero` bucket, so multiplier() can only return 0/1/2/4, dark's psychic immunity is missing, fairy→fairy is fabricated as 2x, and relation()'s 'superweak' branch (:114) is unreachable dead code.
- MatchupMatrix renders attacker-vs-this-Pokemon results under inverted headings (PokemonDetail.tsx:277-294): super-effective attackers appear under 'Strong Against' and 'Weak To' always reads 'None'.
- Evolution chains are keyed by pokemon id rather than species.evolution_chain.url (useData.ts:44-45), showing an unrelated family; flattenEvos (PokemonDetail.tsx:382-393) also collapses branching chains into one linear arrow sequence and reads only evolution_details[0].
- Hardcoded 1010 cap at worker.ts:76, poke.ts:52, Dex.tsx:12 and PokemonDetail.tsx:248 permanently omits species 1011-1025.
- The Worker's /api/type-chart fan-out (worker.ts:85-97) is fetched and discarded — TypeChart.tsx uses it only as a loading gate and computes every cell from the broken local table.
- Proxy failures are returned as HTTP 200 with an {error} body (worker.ts:102-105 + json() hardcoding status 200 at :58), which defeats the client's only guard (`if (!res.ok) throw`, api.ts:8) and lets an error object flow into the UI as data.
- Geometry and token bugs: RadarChart.tsx:15 steps by Math.PI/n instead of 2*Math.PI/n (150° fan, not a hexagon); StatBars.tsx:10-11 duplicates the same hex for two tiers; Dex.tsx:116-128 romanize() overruns its `chars` string so every generation option reads 'Gen undefined'.
- Rot: `hono` is a dependency the Worker never imports, patch-worker.cjs is wired to no npm script and its replacement literals no longer match src/worker.ts (so run_worker_first:true still stands at wrangler.jsonc:11, putting a Worker invocation in front of every static asset), src/ui/Sprite.tsx — the one file with an onError fallback chain — is imported by nothing, and gen1Sprite (poke.ts:71-72) builds a `front_default/` path that 404s for all 1010 ids.
- Accessibility is near-absent: two real aria-labels in the whole app plus a no-op aria-label="" (Card.tsx:31), no label on the search input or generation select, no aria-current/aria-pressed on nav tabs or toggles, no prefers-reduced-motion guard for the fadeup animation (index.css:50-56); and the browse grid overflows a 360px viewport.

## Standout

src/worker.ts:29-54 — a properly built KV edge cache (json-typed get, upstream error propagation, non-blocking waitUntil put with a 6MB serialization guard and configurable TTL, x-cache reporting) that genuinely works. It is the one part of this submission that is both complete and correct, and it makes the wasted /api/type-chart fan-out and the wrong evolution-chain keys above it that much more of a shame.
